The discussion addresses the campaign's electoral impact and the broader themes of election integrity, legal challenges, and public communication amid voter deletion controversies. Madurai Temple Power Cut Sparks Row as EPS Slams Government; Minister Cries Foul
A political confrontation has broken out in Tamil Nadu following a power outage at the Madurai Meenakshi Amman Temple while former Chief Minister Edappadi K. Palaniswami was offering prayers. Portions of the historic shrine were plunged into darkness for seven to eight minutes before electricity was restored. Following his visit, Palaniswami strongly criticised the administration, stating that people are unable even to pray peacefully under the present government. Addressing the incident, Tamil Nadu Electricity Minister C. T. R. Nirmal Kumar clarified that maintenance activities and generator switchovers were underway due to multiple VIP visits. However, he also alleged deliberate foul play within the department, claiming miscreants purposefully disrupt electricity supply during VIP movements. The minister confirmed that internal transfers, meetings, and suspensions are being initiated to probe the lapse and address intentional sabotage.
Nayab Saini Attacks Rahul Gandhi Over 1984 Riots Ahead of November 1 Rally
Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots ahead of the INDIA bloc rally scheduled for November 1 in Delhi. Saini accused the Congress of vitiating the atmosphere of the country and questioned whether Rahul Gandhi's outreach initiative would account for the destruction of homes and shops during the 1984 violence, specifically citing events in Haryana under past Congress rule.
Karnataka Hikes Nandini Milk Price by ₹8, BJP Slams Move, Hotel Association Flags Rising Food Costs
The Karnataka government has decided to increase the price of Nandini milk by eight rupees per litre, with the revised rates scheduled to take effect from November 1. Under the new pricing structure, the cost will rise from forty-six rupees to fifty-four rupees per litre. According to the government, seven rupees of the total hike will go directly to dairy farmers reeling under drought and rising input costs, while one rupee will be allocated to the Milk Federation. The decision has sparked intense political debate, with the opposition BJP slamming the Congress-led government for burdening poor and middle-class citizens and mismanaging the state's finances. Meanwhile, the Bengaluru Hotels Association has raised concerns over the steep revision, cautioning that it will inevitably drive up the prices of tea, coffee, and daily food items for consumers across Karnataka.
India's Inequality Drops Sharply as Extreme Poverty Falls to 2.6%: World Bank
A latest World Bank report reveals a historic decline in India's inequality, with the Gini index falling to 23.5 in 2026, placing India among low inequality nations globally in consumption terms. Extreme poverty in the country dropped significantly from 27.6% to 2.6%. Additionally, the proportion of citizens earning less than 400 rupees per day decreased from 57.7% to 16.1%. Analysts note that while these percentages represent a major achievement, absolute population numbers still highlight ongoing developmental challenges alongside domestic economic growth.
